seen.where: Yale finding aid https://ead-pdfs.library.yale.edu/11076.pdf (Spinelli archive, GEN MSS 109), PDF pp. 105 and 125; no scan online
seen.extent: b. 126 f. 2560-65: Piero Spinelli, 30 letters, 90 pp. part in cipher, 1514-26; Barcelona letter of 7 Sep 1519, 4 pp. part in cipher
seen.cipher: Finding aid: 'Spinelli, Piero. 30 letters; Anversa (Antwerp), Bruggia (Bruges), Rignalla, Venezia (Venice). 90pp. part in cipher. 1514-26' and 'Barchenonia (Barcelona). 4pp. part in cipher. 1519 Sep 7'. A 2017 blog post (Schmeh) shows a Beinecke letter from Tommaso in Barcelona to Leonardo Spinelli with two ciphered paragraphs, very probably the 1519 Barcelona letter, so cipher text survives there; the Piero letters are known only from the finding aid.

prior_art.edition: No printed edition of the Spinelli family letters found. Domnina, 'Ciphers in Early Tudor Diplomacy: the Case of Tommaso Spinelli's Private Letters' (Geheime Post, 2015, pp. 181-194, DHI Paris catalogue) studies Tommaso's private-letter cipher; full text not opened (the Lomonosov PDF did not answer).
prior_art.literature: Per commenters on the 2017 Schmeh blog post, Domnina 2015 prints a cipher table (p. 186) and an improved key; Norbert read page 1 ('et li dite che madama...') and Thomas part of page 2, so a partial decipherment of the Barcelona letter is on record. Nothing found on Piero Spinelli's cipher.

2110.closed: The 7 Sep 1519 Barcelona letter (Tommaso to Leonardo Spinelli) has a decipherment on record: Domnina's 2015 key and partial readings of pages 1-2 posted in the comments of Schmeh's blog post of 24 Mar 2017 (scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/03/24). The 30 Piero Spinelli letters (f. 2560-65) were not found studied; split them into their own lead if a scan can be had.

And then be well', obtained for Count Rumyantsev by a Foreign Ministry clerk who wrote the names and monosyllables under each other and read the first letters (an acrostic).
